title: Normalized Koszul duality agrees with the intrinsic determinant under polynomial refinements
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and fix $d\geq0$. Suppose $X$ has an open cover by factorizations $U\xrightarrow{i}P\to S$, where $P$ is open in $\mathbf A^n_S$ and $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal $I$ is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence of length $c=n-d$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Assume $C_i=I/I^2$, regarded on $U$, is locally free of rank $c$. Put $V_i=i^*\Omega^1_{P/S}$, $E_i=[C_i\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}V_i]$ in degrees $-1,0$, and $D_i=(\bigwedge^c C_i)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^nV_i$, with $\vee=\mathcal Hom(-,\mathcal O_U)$. Pullbacks, differentials, exterior powers and sheaf duals use [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Let $L=L_{X/S}$ with its canonical conormal comparisons $\lambda_i:E_i\simeq L|_U$ be the cotangent complex of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation], and use the determinant functor of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant]. There is a canonical isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_P)$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-derived-internal-hom], respecting the natural $i_*\mathcal O_U$-action,
$$\rho_i:R\mathcal Hom_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S})\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*D_i[-c].$$
It is the signed dual Koszul comparison tensored with the ambient line $\Omega^n_{P/S}$; its top determinant pairing uses the ordered Koszul contractions, including their cohomological signs. It is independent of regular generators and of the trivialization of the ambient line, and commutes with open restriction. After the shift $[n]$, the comparisons between the polynomial duality models $R\mathcal Hom_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S}[n])$, viewed as complexes on $U$, correspond under $\rho_i[n]$ to $\det(\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i)[d]$. In particular this assertion includes the elementary polynomial refinement adjoining a coordinate $t$ whose image is the image of $a\in\mathcal O_P$: the extra equation $t-a$ and differential $\mathrm d(t-a)=\mathrm dt-\mathrm da$ give the acyclic summand $[\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_U]$, and its comparison is evaluation, sending the dual of $t-a$ tensored with $\mathrm d(t-a)$ to $1$. The assertion holds for combined-coordinate refinements and their compositions, with the same ordered wedge and cohomological signs. If moreover $S$ is locally Noetherian (covered by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) and $f$ is separated, flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], these maps identify the normalized relative dualizing object $D_f$ of [lem-trf-relative-duality-polynomial-chart] globally with $\det(L_{X/S})[d]$, with precisely its specified polynomial-chart comparisons. No relative dualizing object is assumed to exist in the unconditional part of the assertion.

proof.text: Work locally on $P$ where the ideal has Koszul-regular generators $g_1,\ldots,g_c$ and $\omega=\Omega^n_{P/S}$ is trivial. The finite free Koszul resolution computes the derived Hom by [lem-sc-derived-hom-finite-free-model]. Apply [lem-sc-koszul-regular-sequence-dual-complex] and its determinant normalization [def-sc-koszul-conormal-comparison]. Tensoring this finite Hom complex with the free rank-one coefficient $\omega$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(K(g),\omega)$. Its comparison is zero except in degree $c$, where a functional $z$ maps to the element whose pairing with $\bar g_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar g_c$ is $s_c\overline{z(e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_c)}$, with $s_c=(-1)^{c(c-1)/2}$. On a conormal basis the determinant pairing identifies $\bigwedge^c C_i^\vee$ with $(\bigwedge^c C_i)^\vee$: both have the dual top basis, so this is an isomorphism including $c=0$. This constructs the local $\rho_i$ with ambient-line coefficients and gives vanishing outside degree $c$.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ (lemma-regular-immersion-ext), signed local dual Koszul computation; conormal basis: more-algebra.tex Tags 0CEM, 062I.

proof.text: For a second Koszul-regular generating tuple, [lem-sc-koszul-ext-determinant-roof] gives the same normalized top Ext map on every quotient-augmented Koszul roof. Thus the local maps of step 1 agree on top cohomology. Changing a frame $w$ of $\omega$ to $uw$ multiplies both the Hom coefficient and the determinant target by $u$; hence their comparison also agrees. Localization preserves the Koszul comparison by [lem-sc-koszul-regular-sequence-dual-complex], and [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open] identifies restriction of the derived Hom itself. The top-cohomology maps therefore glue as module-sheaf maps on $P$. Outside $U$ the source is zero (its first argument is zero) and the target is zero. No Noetherian or quasi-compact hypothesis has entered.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ (lemma-regular-immersion-ext), intrinsic top Ext identification; cohomology.tex Tag 08DL (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U).

proof.text: Keep the quotient-algebra action throughout. In sheaf coinduction it is precomposition by multiplication, by [lem-sc-sheaf-coinduction-adjunction]; computing its right derived functor with injectives retains this action. The local top map in step 1 is $\mathcal O_U$-linear by the quotient-linearity clause of [lem-sc-koszul-regular-sequence-dual-complex]. Let $J$ represent this coinduced complex over $i_*\mathcal O_U$. Its cohomology is zero except in degree $c$. There is an explicit canonical roof $J\leftarrow\tau_{\leq c}J\to H^c(J)[-c]$: the left map is inclusion, and the right map is the quotient $\ker d^c\to\ker d^c/\operatorname{im}d^{c-1}$ in degree $c$, zero elsewhere. Both are quasi-isomorphisms by the cohomology formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Compose this roof with the glued top map of step 2. It gives the required global derived isomorphism over the quotient algebra, hence also in $D(\mathcal O_P)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], after shifting, two such maps are equal exactly when their degree-$c$ sheaf maps are equal. This proves generator independence and restriction compatibility for the derived comparison, not just for its cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ; modules.tex Tag 0A6F (lemma-adjoint-tensor-restrict); derived.tex Tag 05RU and Tag 06XS (lemma-negative-exts).

proof.text: Consider one refinement on an affine base: $P$ is a localization of $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, $B=P/I$, $Q=P[t]$, $h=t-a$, and $Q\to B$ sends $t$ to $\bar a$. The two-term complex $K(h)$ resolves $P$: multiplication by the monic $h$ is injective by its highest coefficient, and its cokernel is evaluation at $a$. The ordered complex $K_Q(g_1,\ldots,g_c,h)$ is the tensor of $K_P(g)\otimes_PQ$ with $K(h)$; the alternating differential formula of [lem-weil-pbc-koszul-differential] verifies this on basis wedges. The cone coordinates of [lem-weil-pbc-koszul-tensor-cone-coordinates] identify it with the cone of multiplication by $t-a$. Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to its cone triangle: its homology is the kernel and cokernel of $t-a$ on $B[t]$, namely zero and $B$. Here $K_P(g)\otimes_PQ$ resolves $B[t]$ because it is a direct sum, coefficient by coefficient, of copies of $K_P(g)$. Thus the enlarged equations are Koszul-regular, without a Noetherian assumption. Their conormal basis is $(\bar g_1,\ldots,\bar g_c,\bar h)$ by [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis].

source.place: dualizing.tex Tag 0BZJ (lemma-well-defined), one-variable reduction; more-algebra.tex Tags 0622, 0629.

proof.text: Write $\eta=\mathrm dt-\mathrm da$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], $(\mathrm dx_1,\ldots,\mathrm dx_n,\eta)$ is a basis: the change from $\mathrm dt$ is triangular with diagonal $1$. In these bases the refined conormal complex is $E_Q=E_P\oplus[B\bar h\xrightarrow{1}B\eta]$. The presentation map $Q\to P$, $t\mapsto a$, is the projection killing $\bar h$ and $\eta$. Naturality in [lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model], followed by the lci identification in [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation], says precisely that this projection represents $\lambda_P^{-1}\lambda_Q$. In particular this is the specified cotangent comparison, rather than an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism between the same two objects.

Define the polynomial-duality comparison by composing coinduction and evaluating the $h$-factor. Derived transposition is available without Noetherian hypotheses by [lem-trf-derived-bimodule-tensor-hom] and [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction]: twice transposing a morphism along $Q\to P\to B$ gives the same Hom bijection as transposing along $Q\to B$, since $B\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P=B$. For the coefficient, the length-one calculation of step 1 gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_Q(P,Q)=P\bar h^\vee[-1]$. Tensor with the free coefficient $\Omega^{n+1}_{Q/R}$, and send $\bar h^\vee\otimes\eta$ to $1$. After $[n+1]$ this is $R\operatorname{Hom}_Q(P,\Omega^{n+1}_{Q/R}[n+1])\simeq\Omega^n_{P/R}[n]$. Apply $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(B,-)$. These are exactly the boundary/evaluation maps defining the refinement in [def-trf-polynomial-duality-presentation-data]. This constructs the unconditional comparison directly; it does not apply a Noetherian duality existence theorem to $R$.

source.place: Tag 0BZJ (lemma-well-defined), effective-Cartier step; Tag 0BZH (lemma-compute-for-effective-Cartier-algebraic); dga.tex Tags 09LN, 09LT.

proof.text: Check the signs in step 6 before comparing determinants. Put $w=\mathrm dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\mathrm dx_n$, and write $e_g^*$ and $e_{g,h}^*$ for the raw functionals of value $1$ on the ordered top wedges. The Hom differential is $d(z)=(-1)^{q+1}z d_K$ in degree $q$ [def-sc-koszul-dual-complex]. Currying on the ordered tensor resolution is the complex isomorphism of [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total]. With the old volume placed before $\eta$, the shift/tensor interchange in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] moves the degree-one $h$ contraction past the shift $[n]$, giving $(-1)^n$. Thus the refined-to-old map on raw top classes is $e_{g,h}^*\otimes(w\wedge\eta)\mapsto(-1)^n e_g^*\otimes w$. The normalized comparisons instead send these raw classes to $s_{c+1}(\bar g\wedge\bar h)^\vee\otimes(w\wedge\eta)$ and $s_c\bar g^\vee\otimes w$. Since $s_{c+1}=(-1)^c s_c$, the induced map between normalized determinant generators is multiplication by $(-1)^{n+c}$. This retains the total-Hom differential signs; treating the raw top functional as the ordered contraction would lose $(-1)^c$.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ (lemma-regular-immersion-ext), ordered contractions and sign warning; dualizing.tex Tags 0BZI, 0BZJ; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A90.

proof.text: The determinant comparison for the projection in step 5 gives the same scalar. On affine charts the determinant functor acts on a derived isomorphism by the kernel-normalized good-diagram map of [lem-trf-affine-two-term-determinant], so for this degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism it is the map $T$ of [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus]. The kernel is $[B\bar h\xrightarrow{1}B\eta]$. In the kernel-first short exact sequence maps of [lem-trf-surjective-two-term-determinant-calculus], moving $\bar h$ from the last position to the first contributes $(-1)^c$ to the conormal top wedge, and moving $\eta$ from last to first contributes $(-1)^n$ to the ambient top wedge. The inverse dual has the same sign. The kernel determinant is trivialized by evaluation, as specified by [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant]. Hence the appended-generator determinant is multiplied by $(-1)^{n+c}$, exactly step 7. If kernel-first wedges are used throughout, both maps are simply evaluation $\bar h^\vee\otimes\eta\mapsto1$. This proves the one-coordinate assertion with its specified signs. Since both sides are shifted lines, equality on these top generators is equality of derived maps by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful].

source.place: more-algebra.tex Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), kernel-first construction; Tag 0FJM; perfect.tex Tag 0FJX.

proof.text: If a different lift $a'$ is used, write $a'-a=\sum b_jg_j$. The new last equation is $h'=h-\sum b_jg_j$; on the conormal this is an elementary triangular change of enlarged generators with determinant $1$. On $U$, $\mathrm dh'=\mathrm dh-\sum\bar b_j\mathrm dg_j$, since the $g_j$ vanish. The two projections from the enlarged conormal complex to $E_P$ differ by the chain homotopy $H$ sending $\mathrm dt$ to $\sum\bar b_j\bar g_j$ and all $\mathrm dx_k$ to $0$: in degree $-1$ their difference is $H\mathrm d$, and in degree $0$ it is $\mathrm dH$. Thus they give the same derived map, using the homotopy localization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and their determinants agree by [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant]. The normalized-roof formula [lem-sc-koszul-ext-determinant-roof] identifies step 1 for the two enlarged tuples. Step 8 therefore identifies the two duality comparisons with this same determinant map. Shifted single-complex faithfulness makes this equality an equality of derived maps over $B$.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ, generator-independent normalized roof; dualizing.tex Tag 0BZJ, choice of the lift in a polynomial refinement.

proof.text: Adjoin finitely many coordinates one at a time and compose steps 5--9. This is an induction starting with the identity refinement, where there is no extra equation and both maps are the identity. At each step the remaining old equations are Koszul-regular by step 4, so the next application is legitimate. Composition of the determinant maps is the functor law of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant]. Composition of the duality maps is composition of the transpositions of step 6; on three factors their adjunct is evaluation at $1$ in all factors in either parenthesization, so the adjunction bijection makes them equal. Exchanging two new equations negates their conormal wedge and exchanging their two new differentials negates the ambient wedge, so their product is unchanged; the corresponding interchange of the two degree-one contractions has exactly the tensor Koszul sign by [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total]. Thus the calculation includes arbitrary ordered combined-coordinate refinements, not just one chosen order.

source.place: Tag 0BZJ (lemma-well-defined), reduction by induction to one added variable; Tag 0BZI top-differential footnote.

proof.text: For two polynomial presentations of the same affine part of $U$, adjoin the coordinate tuple of the second to the first, choosing lifts of its images, and conversely. This gives the combined-coordinate presentation $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_m]\to B$ (localized where required). Both routes have Koszul-regular equations by step 4. The conormal projection maps commute with the intrinsic $\lambda$ by step 5, so their ratio in the derived category is $\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i$. Steps 8--10 identify the ratio of duality maps with the determinant of this ratio. Localizations agree by step 2; cover general overlaps by these affine restrictions instead of asserting that an overlap is affine. Maps between the shifted lines are ordinary maps of sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], so their equality on this cover proves equality globally. The passage between a chart with its quotient-algebra action and its object on $U$ is the affine-morphism derived equivalence of [lem-sc-finite-affine-derived-equivalence], applied to the closed immersion. This yields precisely $\det(\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i)[d]$, since $n-c=d$, and the functor law supplies all composition compatibilities.

source.place: Tag 0BZJ (lemma-well-defined), combined-coordinate square; cotangent.tex Tags 08RB, 08SL; perfect.tex Tag 0FJX.

proof.text: Finally assume $S$ locally Noetherian and $f$ separated, flat and locally of finite presentation. These are exactly the additional hypotheses of [lem-trf-relative-duality-polynomial-chart], so it supplies $D_f$ with the specified normalized model comparisons. The global determinant $\det L$ and its local exterior identifications are supplied by [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant], applied to the models in [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation]. On each chart step 3 shifted by $[n]$ gives the map to $D_i[d]$; step 11 identifies its overlaps with the determinant transitions. Hence the maps to $\det L[d]$ agree on overlaps. Locally both objects are sheaves shifted by $d$; the explicit truncation roof of step 3 identifies them globally with their degree $-d$ cohomology sheaves shifted by $d$. Their ordinary sheaf maps therefore glue to an isomorphism $D_f\simeq\det L[d]$. Its chart maps are the ones constructed above, so it has the required normalization. For $c=0$ the Koszul complex and $s_c$ are $\mathcal O$ and $1$; for empty charts everything is zero. The preceding proof also covers $d=0$, $n=0$, nonreduced bases and nonseparated overlaps. The extra dualizing hypotheses were used only in this last step.
